first: अस्य श्रीललितासहस्रनामस्तोत्रमाला मन्त्रस्य वशिन्यादि वाग्देवता ऋषयः ।
en: For this hymn, the garland of Lalita's thousand names, the seers are the goddesses of speech led by Vashini, the metre is anushtup, and the deity is Shri Lalita, the supreme goddess. The vagbhava part of her mantra is the seed, the middle part is the power, and the shakti part is the key. It is used in japa to gain the fruit one wishes for, through the grace of Lalita Mahatripurasundari; one then offers the five-fold worship that begins with 'lam'.

Meditate on the supreme Mother. Her body is red like vermilion, she has three eyes, her ruby crown shines with the moon on it, she smiles, and her breasts are full. In her hands she holds a jewelled cup full of nectar and a red lotus; she is gentle, and her red feet rest on a jewelled pot.

She is the holy Mother (Shrimata), the great Queen (Shrimaharajni), the ruler of the glorious lion throne (Shrimatsimhasaneshvari). She rose from the fire-pit of pure consciousness (Chidagnikunda-sambhuta) and is ready to do the work of the gods (Devakarya-samudyata).

She shines like a thousand rising suns (Udyadbhanu-sahasrabha) and has four arms (Chaturbahu-samanvita). She holds the noose that is desire (Ragasvarupa-pashadhya) and shines with the goad that is anger (Krodhakarankushojjvala).

Her sugarcane bow is the mind (Manorupekshu-kodanda) and her five arrows are the five subtle elements (Panchatanmatra-sayaka). The whole universe is bathed in the flood of her own red light (Nijaruna-prabhapura-majjad-brahmanda-mandala).

Her hair shines with champaka, ashoka, punnaga and saugandhika flowers (Champakashoka-punnaga-saugandhika-lasatkacha). She wears a crown glittering with rows of rubies (Kuruvinda-mani-shreni-kanatkotira-mandita).

Her forehead shines like the half moon of the eighth night (Ashtamichandra-vibhraja-dalikasthala-shobhita). The musk mark on her face looks like the dark spot on the moon (Mukhachandra-kalankabha-mriganabhi-visheshaka).

Her eyebrows are like the arched gate of the house of Kama, which is her face (Vadanasmara-mangalya-grihatorana-chillika). Her eyes move like fish in the flowing stream of her face's beauty (Vaktralakshmi-parivaha-chalanminabha-lochana).
Her nose is lovely like a fresh champaka bud (Navachampaka-pushpabha-nasadanda-virajita). Her nose jewel shines brighter than the stars (Tarakanti-tiraskari-nasabharana-bhasura).
She is lovely with ear ornaments made of kadamba flower clusters (Kadambamanjari-klripta-karnapura-manohara). The sun and the moon are her pair of earrings (Tatanka-yugali-bhuta-tapanodupa-mandala).

Her cheeks are brighter than mirrors of ruby (Padmaragashiladarsha-paribhavi-kapolabhuh). Her lips are more beautiful than fresh coral and the red bimba fruit (Navavidruma-bimbashri-nyakkari-radanachchhada).

Her two rows of teeth shine like the first shoots of pure knowledge (Shuddhavidyankurakara-dvijapankti-dvayojjvala). The scent of the camphor betel she chews fills every direction (Karpuravitikamoda-samakarshi-digantara).

The sweetness of her speech puts to shame the vina of Sarasvati (Nija-sallapa-madhurya-vinirbhartsita-kachchhapi). The mind of Kameshvara is bathed in the light of her soft smile (Mandasmita-prabhapura-majjat-kamesha-manasa).

She shines with the beauty of a chin that has no equal (Anakalita-sadrishya-chubukashri-virajita). Her neck is graced by the wedding thread tied by Kameshvara (Kamesha-baddha-mangalya-sutra-shobhita-kandhara).
Her lovely arms wear golden armlets (Kanakangada-keyura-kamaniya-bhujanvita). She wears a jewelled necklace with a locket and swinging pearls (Ratnagraiveya-chintaka-lola-mukta-phalanvita).

Her breasts are what she gives Kameshvara in return for the jewel of his love (Kameshvara-premaratna-mani-pratipana-stani). They are like two fruits on the creeper of fine hair that rises from her navel (Nabhyalavala-romali-lata-phala-kuchadvayi).
Her waist is so slender that it can only be guessed from the fine line of hair that rests on it (Lakshyaroma-lata-dharata-samunneya-madhyama).
Her waist has three folds, like a belt holding it as it bends under the weight of her breasts (Stanabhara-dalanmadhya-pattabandha-valitraya).

Her hips shine in a cloth dyed deep red like the dawn (Arunaruna-kausumbha-vastra-bhasvat-katitati). She is adorned with a lovely girdle of small jewelled bells (Ratna-kinkinika-ramya-rashana-dama-bhushita).
The beauty and softness of her thighs is known only to Kameshvara (Kamesha-jnata-saubhagya-mardavoru-dvayanvita). Her knees are shaped like crowns of ruby (Manikya-mukutakara-janudvaya-virajita).

Her calves are like Kama's quivers, dotted with red indragopa insects (Indragopa-parikshipta-smaratunabha-janghika). Her ankles are hidden (Gudhagulpha) and the arches of her feet are curved more finely than a tortoise's back (Kurmaprishtha-jayishnu-prapadanvita).

The light of her toenails removes the inner darkness of those who bow to her (Nakhadidhiti-sanchhanna-namajjana-tamoguna). The glow of her two feet defeats the lotus (Padadvaya-prabhajala-parakrita-saroruha).

Her holy lotus feet are adorned with tinkling jewelled anklets (Shinjana-manimanjira-mandita-shripadambuja). She walks slowly like a swan (Marali-mandagamana) and is a treasure of great beauty (Mahalavanya-shevadhih).

She is red all over (Sarvaruna), her body is flawless (Anavadyangi), and she wears every ornament (Sarvabharana-bhushita). She sits on the lap of Shiva Kameshvara (Shiva-kameshvarankastha), she is auspicious (Shiva), and her beloved is in her own power (Svadhina-vallabha).

She lives on the middle peak of Mount Sumeru (Sumeru-madhya-shringastha) and is the lady of the holy city (Shrimannagara-nayika). She lives in the house of wish-granting jewels (Chintamani-grihantastha) and sits on a seat made of the five Brahmas (Panchabrahmasana-sthita).

She lives in the great lotus forest (Mahapadmatavi-samstha) and in the kadamba grove (Kadambavana-vasini). She dwells in the middle of the ocean of nectar (Sudhasagara-madhyastha); she has loving eyes (Kamakshi) and grants wishes (Kamadayini).

Her glory is praised by crowds of gods and sages (Devarshi-gana-sanghata-stuyamanatma-vaibhava). She is joined by an army of Shaktis ready to kill the demon Bhanda (Bhandasura-vadhodyukta-shaktisena-samanvita).

She is served by a herd of elephants led by Sampatkari (Sampatkari-samarudha-sindhura-vraja-sevita). She is surrounded by countless horses led by Ashvarudha (Ashvarudhadhishthitashva-koti-kotibhir-avrita).

She stands on the chariot Chakraraja, armed with every weapon (Chakraraja-ratharudha-sarvayudha-parishkrita). She is served by Mantrini, who rides the chariot Geyachakra (Geyachakra-ratharudha-mantrini-parisevita).

Dandanatha, riding the chariot Kirichakra, goes before her (Kirichakra-ratharudha-dandanatha-puraskrita). She stands inside the wall of fire raised by Jvalamalini (Jvalamalinikakshipta-vahniprakara-madhyaga).

She is glad at the valour of the Shaktis set on destroying Bhanda's army (Bhandasainya-vadhodyukta-shakti-vikrama-harshita). She is eager to watch the strength and spirit of the Nitya goddesses (Nitya-parakramatopa-nirikshana-samutsuka).

She delights in the valour of Bala, who set out to kill Bhanda's sons (Bhandaputra-vadhodyukta-bala-vikrama-nandita). She is pleased that Mantrini killed the demon Vishanga (Mantrinyamba-virachita-vishanga-vadha-toshita).

She delights in the strength of Varahi, who took the life of Vishukra (Vishukra-pranaharana-varahi-virya-nandita). She brought forth Ganesha just by looking at Kameshvara's face (Kameshvara-mukhaloka-kalpita-shriganeshvara).

She is glad when Mahaganesha breaks the demon's device of obstacles (Mahaganesha-nirbhinna-vighnayantra-praharshita), and she rains a counter-weapon on every weapon Bhandasura throws (Bhandasurendra-nirmukta-shastra-pratyastra-varshini). The ten forms of Narayana came from her fingernails (Karanguli-nakhotpanna-narayana-dashakritih), and she burned the demon soldiers with the fire of the great Pashupata missile (Mahapashupatastragni-nirdagdhasura-sainika).

With the Kameshvara missile she burned Bhandasura together with his city Shunyaka (Kameshvarastra-nirdagdha-sabhandasura-shunyaka). Her glory is praised by Brahma, Vishnu, Indra and the other gods (Brahmopendra-mahendradi-deva-samstuta-vaibhava).

She is the life-giving herb that brought back Kama, who was burned by the fire of Shiva's eye (Hara-netragni-sandagdha-kama-sanjivanaushadhih). Her lotus face is the holy vagbhava part of her mantra (Shrimad-vagbhava-kutaika-svarupa-mukha-pankaja).

Her body from below the neck to the waist is the middle part of the mantra (Kanthadhah-kati-paryanta-madhyakuta-svarupini). Her body below the waist is the shakti part (Shaktikutaikatapanna-katyadhobhaga-dharini).

She is the root mantra itself (Mulamantratmika) and her body is its three parts (Mulakutatraya-kalevara). She alone enjoys the nectar of the Kula path (Kulamritaika-rasika) and guards its secret rules (Kulasanketa-palini).

She is the noble lady of the Kula (Kulangana), dwells within the Kula (Kulantastha), and is Kaulini and Kulayogini. She is also beyond the Kula (Akula), lives within the Samaya path (Samayantastha), and is devoted to its practice (Samayachara-tatpara).

She lives in the Muladhara (Muladharaika-nilaya) and breaks the knot of Brahma (Brahmagranthi-vibhedini). She rises in the Manipura (Manipurantar-udita) and breaks the knot of Vishnu (Vishnugranthi-vibhedini).

She stays in the Ajna chakra (Ajnachakrantaralastha) and breaks the knot of Rudra (Rudragranthi-vibhedini). She climbs to the thousand-petalled lotus (Sahasrarambujarudha) and pours down streams of nectar (Sudhasarabhivarshini).

She shines like a streak of lightning (Tadillata-samaruchih) and rests above the six chakras (Shatchakropari-samsthita). She is the great power (Mahashaktih), the coiled Kundalini, and as fine as a lotus fibre (Bisatantu-taniyasi).

She is Bhavani, reached through meditation (Bhavanagamya), and an axe for the forest of worldly life (Bhavaranya-kutharika). She loves what is good (Bhadrapriya), is goodness in form (Bhadramurti), and gives good fortune to devotees (Bhakta-saubhagyadayini).

She loves devotion (Bhaktipriya), is reached by devotion (Bhaktigamya), is won by devotion (Bhaktivashya), and takes away fear (Bhayapaha). She is Shambhavi, worshipped by Sharada (Sharadaradhya), Sharvani, and the giver of happiness (Sharmadayini).

She is Shankari, the giver of wealth (Shrikari), the good woman (Sadhvi), with a face like the autumn moon (Sharachchandra-nibhanana). She is slender-waisted (Shatodari), full of peace (Shantimati), without support (Niradhara) and spotless (Niranjana).

She is untouched (Nirlepa), pure (Nirmala), eternal (Nitya), formless (Nirakara) and untroubled (Nirakula). She is beyond qualities (Nirguna), without parts (Nishkala), calm (Shanta), without desire (Nishkama) and free from harm (Nirupaplava).

She is always free (Nityamukta), unchanging (Nirvikara), beyond the world (Nishprapancha) and needs no support (Nirashraya). She is ever pure (Nityashuddha), ever awake (Nityabuddha), faultless (Niravadya) and without break (Nirantara).

She has no cause (Nishkarana), no stain (Nishkalanka), no limit (Nirupadhi) and no lord above her (Nirishvara). She is free of attachment (Niraga) and destroys attachment (Ragamathani); she is free of pride (Nirmada) and destroys pride (Madanashini).

She is free of worry (Nishchinta), of ego (Nirahankara) and of delusion (Nirmoha), and she destroys delusion (Mohanashini). She has no sense of 'mine' (Nirmama) and removes it (Mamatahantri); she is sinless (Nishpapa) and destroys sin (Papanashini).

She is without anger (Nishkrodha) and calms anger (Krodhashamani); without greed (Nirlobha) and destroys greed (Lobhanashini). She is without doubt (Nihsamshaya) and kills doubt (Samshayaghni); she is without birth (Nirbhava) and ends the round of births (Bhavanashini).

She is beyond all mental pictures (Nirvikalpa), without hindrance (Nirabadha), without division (Nirbheda), and removes division (Bhedanashini). She is imperishable (Nirnasha), destroys death (Mrityumathani), is beyond action (Nishkriya) and owns nothing (Nishparigraha).

She has no equal (Nistula), has dark hair (Nilachikura), is free of danger (Nirapaya) and cannot be passed beyond (Niratyaya). She is hard to win (Durlabha), hard to reach (Durgama), Durga, the remover of sorrow (Duhkhahantri) and the giver of happiness (Sukhaprada).

She is far from the wicked (Dushtadura), stops wrong conduct (Durachara-shamani), and has no fault (Doshavarjita). She knows everything (Sarvajna), is full of deep compassion (Sandrakaruna), and has no equal or superior (Samanadhika-varjita).

She holds all powers (Sarvashaktimayi), is fully auspicious (Sarvamangala), and gives the good path (Sadgatiprada). She is the ruler of all (Sarveshvari), she is everything (Sarvamayi), she is all mantras (Sarvamantrasvarupini) and all forms (Sarvarupini).

She is all yantras (Sarvayantratmika), all tantras (Sarvatantrarupa), and the state beyond the mind (Manonmani). She is Maheshvari, the great goddess (Mahadevi), Mahalakshmi, and the beloved of Shiva (Mridapriya).

She has a great form (Maharupa), is most worthy of worship (Mahapujya), and destroys great sins (Mahapataka-nashini). She is the great illusion (Mahamaya), great in goodness (Mahasattva), the great power (Mahashakti), and great joy (Maharati).

She has great enjoyment (Mahabhoga), great lordship (Mahaishvarya), great valour (Mahavirya) and great strength (Mahabala). She has great wisdom (Mahabuddhi) and great powers (Mahasiddhi), and is the ruler of the lords of yoga (Mahayogeshvareshvari).

She is the great tantra (Mahatantra), the great mantra (Mahamantra), the great yantra (Mahayantra), and has a great seat (Mahasana). She is worshipped by the great rites (Mahayaga-kramaradhya) and by Mahabhairava (Mahabhairava-pujita). She is the witness of Shiva's great dance at the end of the great age (Maheshvara-mahakalpa-mahatandava-sakshini); she is the queen of Mahakameshvara (Mahakamesha-mahishi) and is Mahatripurasundari.

She is honoured with the sixty-four offerings (Chatuhshashtyupacharadhya) and holds the sixty-four arts (Chatuhshashtikalamayi). She is served by the great host of sixty-four crore yoginis (Mahachatuhshashtikoti-yogini-ganasevita).

She is the Vidya of Manu (Manuvidya) and the Vidya of Chandra (Chandravidya), and lives in the centre of the moon's disc (Chandramandala-madhyaga). She has a lovely form (Charurupa), a lovely smile (Charuhasa), and wears a lovely crescent moon (Charuchandra-kaladhara).

She is the ruler of all that moves and does not move (Characharajagannatha) and lives in the Shri Chakra (Chakraraja-niketana). She is Parvati, lotus-eyed (Padmanayana), and shines like a ruby (Padmaraga-samaprabha).

She sits on a seat of five lifeless forms (Panchapretasanasina) and is the five Brahmas (Panchabrahma-svarupini). She is pure consciousness (Chinmayi), supreme bliss (Paramananda), and knowledge itself (Vijnanaghana-rupini).

She is meditation, the one who meditates and the one meditated on (Dhyana-dhyatri-dhyeya-rupa), and she is beyond right and wrong (Dharmadharma-vivarjita). She is the universal form (Vishvarupa), the waking state (Jagarini), the dreaming state (Svapanti), and its inner light (Taijasatmika).

She is deep sleep (Supta) and its knowing self (Prajnatmika), the fourth state (Turya), and beyond all states (Sarvavastha-vivarjita). She creates in the form of Brahma (Srishtikartri, Brahmarupa) and protects in the form of Govinda (Goptri, Govindarupini).

She destroys in the form of Rudra (Samharini, Rudrarupa), and as Ishvari she hides all things (Tirodhanakari). As Sadashiva she gives grace (Anugrahada); she is devoted to these five acts (Panchakritya-parayana).
She lives in the middle of the sun's disc (Bhanumandala-madhyastha) and is Bhairavi and Bhagamalini. She sits on a lotus (Padmasana), is Bhagavati, and is the sister of Vishnu (Padmanabha-sahodari).

Whole worlds arise and vanish as she opens and closes her eyes (Unmesha-nimishotpanna-vipanna-bhuvanavali). She has a thousand heads and faces (Sahasrashirshavadana), a thousand eyes (Sahasrakshi) and a thousand feet (Sahasrapat).

She is the mother of all, from Brahma down to the worm (Abrahmakita-janani), and set up the order of social classes and stages of life (Varnashrama-vidhayini). The Vedas are her own command (Nijajnarupa-nigama), and she gives the fruits of good and bad deeds (Punyapunya-phalaprada).

The dust of her lotus feet is the vermilion in the hair-parting of the Vedas (Shruti-simanta-sindurikrita-padabjadhulika). She is the pearl inside the shell made of all the scriptures (Sakalagama-sandoha-shukti-samputa-mauktika).

She gives the goals of life (Purusharthaprada), is complete (Purna), enjoys all (Bhogini), and rules the worlds (Bhuvaneshvari). She is the Mother (Ambika), without beginning or end (Anadi-nidhana), and is served by Vishnu, Brahma and Indra (Haribrahmendra-sevita).

She is Narayani, her form is sound (Nadarupa), and she is beyond name and form (Namarupa-vivarjita). She is the syllable Hrim (Hrimkari), modest (Hrimati), dear to the heart (Hridya), and beyond what is to be rejected or taken up (Heyopadeya-varjita).

She is worshipped by the king of kings (Rajarajarchita), is the Queen (Rajni), lovely (Ramya) and lotus-eyed (Rajivalochana). She gives delight (Ranjani), charms (Ramani), is full of sweetness (Rasya), and wears a girdle of ringing bells (Ranatkinkini-mekhala).

She is Rama (Lakshmi), with a face like the full moon (Rakenduvadana); she is Rati in form (Ratirupa) and loved by Rati (Ratipriya). She protects (Rakshakari), kills demons (Rakshasaghni), is lovely (Rama), and delights in her beloved (Ramanalampata).

She is desired by all (Kamya), the form of Kamakala (Kamakalarupa), and loves kadamba flowers (Kadambakusuma-priya). She is auspicious (Kalyani), the root of the world (Jagatikanda), and an ocean of compassion (Karunarasa-sagara).

She is full of arts (Kalavati), sweet in speech (Kalalapa), beautiful (Kanta), and fond of the kadambari drink (Kadambari-priya). She grants boons (Varada), has lovely eyes (Vamanayana), and is overcome with the joy of varuni wine (Varunimada-vihvala).

She is above the universe (Vishvadhika), known through the Vedas (Vedavedya), and lives on the Vindhya mountains (Vindhyachala-nivasini). She is the creator (Vidhatri), mother of the Vedas (Vedajanani), Vishnu's power of illusion (Vishnumaya), and full of play (Vilasini).

She is the body, the field (Kshetrasvarupa), the ruler of the field (Kshetreshi), and protects both the field and its knower (Kshetra-kshetrajna-palini). She is free from loss and gain (Kshayavriddhi-vinirmukta) and is worshipped by the guardians of the field (Kshetrapala-samarchita).

She is victorious (Vijaya), pure (Vimala), worthy of worship (Vandya), and loving to those who bow to her (Vandarujana-vatsala). She is the goddess of speech (Vagvadini), has beautiful hair (Vamakeshi), and lives in the circle of fire (Vahnimandala-vasini).

She is a wish-granting creeper for the devoted (Bhaktimat-kalpalatika) and frees bound souls from their bonds (Pashupasha-vimochini). She destroys all false teachings (Samhritashesha-pashanda) and spreads good conduct (Sadachara-pravartika).

She is moonlight that cools those burned by the fire of the three kinds of suffering (Tapatrayagni-santapta-samahladana-chandrika). She is young (Taruni), worshipped by ascetics (Tapasaradhya), slender-waisted (Tanumadhya), and removes darkness (Tamopaha).

She is the true meaning of the words 'chit' and 'tat' (Chitistatpada-lakshyartha) and is pure consciousness alone (Chidekarasa-rupini). The bliss of Brahma and the other gods is only a drop of her own bliss (Svatmananda-lavibhuta-brahmadyananda-santatih).

She is Para, the highest level of speech, and the inner consciousness (Pratyak-chitirupa); she is Pashyanti, the supreme deity (Paradevata), Madhyama and Vaikhari (Vaikharirupa). She is the swan in the minds of her devotees (Bhaktamanasa-hamsika).

She is the life-breath of Kameshvara (Kameshvara-prananadi), grateful (Kritajna), and worshipped by Kama (Kamapujita). She is full of the feeling of love (Shringara-rasa-sampurna), victorious (Jaya), and dwells in Jalandhara (Jalandhara-sthita).

She lives in the holy seat of Odyana (Odyanapitha-nilaya) and in the circle of the bindu (Bindumandala-vasini). She is worshipped by secret rites (Rahoyoga-kramaradhya) and pleased by secret offerings (Rahastarpana-tarpita).

She gives grace at once (Sadyahprasadini), is the witness of the universe (Vishvasakshini), and has no witness over her (Sakshivarjita). She is joined by the deities of the six limbs (Shadangadevata-yukta) and is full of the six divine virtues (Shadgunya-paripurita).

first: नित्या – क्लिन्ना निरुपमा निर्वाण सुख दायिनी ।
en: She is ever tender with mercy (Nityaklinna), beyond compare (Nirupama), and gives the joy of liberation (Nirvanasukha-dayini). She is the sixteen Nitya goddesses (Nityashodashika-rupa) and is half of Shiva's body (Shrikantardha-sharirini).

She is radiant (Prabhavati), light itself (Prabharupa), well known (Prasiddha), and the supreme ruler (Parameshvari). She is the root of nature (Mulaprakriti), the unmanifest (Avyakta), and both manifest and unmanifest (Vyaktavyakta-svarupini).

She is present everywhere (Vyapini), has many forms (Vividhakara), and is both knowledge and ignorance (Vidyavidya-svarupini). She is the moonlight that makes the lily-like eyes of Mahakameshvara bloom (Mahakamesha-nayana-kumudahlada-kaumudi).

She is a line of rising suns that breaks the darkness in her devotees' hearts (Bhaktahardatamobheda-bhanumad-bhanu-santatih). She sent Shiva as her messenger (Shivaduti), is worshipped by Shiva (Shivaradhya), has Shiva's form (Shivamurti), and brings good (Shivankari).

She is dear to Shiva (Shivapriya), devoted to Shiva (Shivapara), loved by the good (Shishteshta), and worshipped by the good (Shishtapujita). She is beyond measure (Aprameya), shines by her own light (Svaprakasha), and is beyond mind and speech (Manovachamagochara).

She is the power of consciousness (Chichchhakti), awareness itself (Chetanarupa), the power in matter (Jadashakti), and matter itself (Jadatmika). She is Gayatri, the sacred utterances (Vyahriti), the twilight prayer (Sandhya), and is served by the twice-born (Dvijabrinda-nishevita).

The principles of creation are her seat (Tattvasana), she is made of them (Tattvamayi), and she lives within the five sheaths (Panchakoshantara-sthita). Her greatness has no limit (Nihsimamahima); she is ever young (Nityayauvana) and full of joyful rapture (Madashalini).

Her eyes are red and rolling with rapture (Madaghurnita-raktakshi) and her cheeks are flushed (Madapatala-gandabhuh). Her body is smeared with sandal paste (Chandanadrava-digdhangi) and she loves champaka flowers (Champeya-kusuma-priya).

She is skilful (Kushala), gentle in form (Komalakara), is Kurukulla, and rules the Kula (Kuleshvari). She lives in the Kulakunda (Kulakundalaya) and is served by those devoted to the Kaula path (Kaulamarga-tatpara-sevita).

She is the mother of Kumara and Ganesha (Kumara-gananathamba), and she is contentment (Tushti), nourishment (Pushti), understanding (Mati) and steadiness (Dhriti). She is peace (Shanti), well-being (Svastimati), beauty (Kanti), joy (Nandini), and destroys obstacles (Vighnanashini).

She is full of light (Tejovati), three-eyed (Trinayana), has restless eyes (Lolakshi), and takes any form she wishes (Kamarupini). She wears garlands (Malini), is Hamsini, the Mother (Mata), and lives on the Malaya mountain (Malayachala-vasini).

She has a lovely face (Sumukhi), is soft like a lotus (Nalini), has fine eyebrows (Subhru), is beautiful (Shobhana), and leads the gods (Suranayika). She is Kalakanthi, full of radiance (Kantimati), stirs creation into motion (Kshobhini), and has a subtle form (Sukshmarupini).

She is Vajreshvari and Vamadevi, and she is untouched by age (Vayovastha-vivarjita). She is the queen of the perfected ones (Siddheshvari), their knowledge (Siddhavidya), their mother (Siddhamata), and is famous (Yashasvini).

She lives in the Vishuddhi chakra (Vishuddhichakra-nilaya), is reddish in colour (Araktavarna) and three-eyed (Trilochana). She holds the khatvanga staff and other weapons (Khatvangadi-praharana) and has one face (Vadanaika-samanvita).

She loves sweet rice pudding (Payasanna-priya), dwells in the skin (Tvakstha), and frightens those of animal nature (Pashuloka-bhayankari). She is surrounded by Amrita and other great powers (Amritadi-mahashakti-samvrita) and is Dakini, their queen (Dakinishvari).

She lives in the Anahata lotus (Anahatabja-nilaya), is dark in colour (Shyamabha), and has two faces (Vadanadvaya). She shines with her tusks, holds a rosary and other things (Damshtrojjvalakshamaladi-dhara), and dwells in the blood (Rudhira-samsthita).

She is surrounded by Kalaratri and other powers (Kalaratryadi-shaktyaugha-vrita) and loves rice cooked with ghee (Snigdhaudana-priya). She grants boons to great heroes (Mahavirendra-varada) and is Rakini the Mother (Rakinyamba-svarupini).

She lives in the Manipura lotus (Manipurabja-nilaya) and has three faces (Vadanatraya-samyuta). She holds the thunderbolt and other weapons (Vajradikayudhopeta) and is surrounded by Damari and other powers (Damaryadibhir-avrita).

She is red in colour (Raktavarna), dwells in the flesh (Mamsanishtha), and loves rice with jaggery (Gudanna-prita-manasa). She gives joy to all devotees (Samastabhakta-sukhada) and is Lakini the Mother (Lakinyamba-svarupini).

She lives in the Svadhishthana lotus (Svadhishthanambujagata) and is lovely with four faces (Chaturvaktra-manohara). She holds the trident and other weapons (Shuladyayudha-sampanna), is yellow in colour (Pitavarna), and very proud (Atigarvita).

She dwells in the fat of the body (Medonishtha), loves honey (Madhuprita), and is joined by Bandhini and other powers (Bandhinyadi-samanvita). She loves curd rice (Dadhyannasakta-hridaya) and takes the form of Kakini (Kakinirupa-dharini).

She sits in the Muladhara lotus (Muladharambujarudha), has five faces (Panchavaktra), and dwells in the bones (Asthisamsthita). She holds the goad and other weapons (Ankushadi-praharana) and is served by Varada and other powers (Varadadi-nishevita).

She loves rice cooked with green gram (Mudgaudanasakta-chitta) and is Sakini the Mother (Sakinyamba-svarupini). She lives in the Ajna chakra lotus (Ajnachakrabja-nilaya), is white (Shuklavarna), and has six faces (Shadanana).

first: मज्जा – संस्था हंसवती – मुख्य – शक्ति – समान्विता ।
en: She dwells in the marrow (Majjasamstha) and is joined by Hamsavati and other chief powers (Hamsavati-mukhyashakti-samanvita). She loves rice cooked with turmeric (Haridrannaika-rasika) and takes the form of Hakini (Hakinirupa-dharini).

She lives in the thousand-petalled lotus (Sahasradala-padmastha) and shines with every colour (Sarvavarnopa-shobhita). She holds every weapon (Sarvayudhadhara), dwells in the vital seed (Shukla-samsthita), and faces every direction (Sarvatomukhi).

She is pleased with every kind of food (Sarvaudana-pritachitta) and is Yakini the Mother (Yakinyamba-svarupini). She is Svaha and Svadha, beyond thought (Amati), intelligence (Medha), the Vedas (Shruti), the law books (Smriti), and the highest (Anuttama).

Her fame is holy (Punyakirti), she is reached through good deeds (Punyalabhya), and to hear and praise her is holy (Punyashravana-kirtana). She is worshipped by Indra's wife (Pulomajarchita), frees from bondage (Bandhamochani), and has lovely curling hair (Bandhuralaka).

She is the power of self-awareness (Vimarsharupini), knowledge (Vidya), and the mother of the world, starting with space (Viyadadi-jagatprasuh). She cures all diseases (Sarvavyadhi-prashamani) and keeps away every kind of death (Sarvamrityu-nivarini).

She is the first of all (Agraganya), her form is beyond thought (Achintyarupa), and she destroys the sins of the Kali age (Kalikalmasha-nashini). She is Katyayani, she destroys time (Kalahantri), and is worshipped by the lotus-eyed Vishnu (Kamalaksha-nishevita).

Her mouth is full of betel (Tambulapurita-mukhi) and she glows like a pomegranate flower (Dadimikusuma-prabha). She is doe-eyed (Mrigakshi), enchanting (Mohini), the chief one (Mukhya), the wife of Shiva (Mridani), and a friend to all (Mitrarupini).

She is ever content (Nityatripta), a treasure for her devotees (Bhaktanidhi), the controller (Niyantri), and the ruler of all (Nikhileshvari). She is reached through friendliness and other good feelings (Maitryadi-vasanalabhya) and is the witness of the great dissolution (Mahapralaya-sakshini).

She is the highest power (Parashakti), the highest goal (Paranishtha), and pure knowledge in form (Prajnanaghana-rupini). She is languid from drinking sweet wine (Madhvipanalasa), rapt (Matta), and her form is the letters of the alphabet (Matrikavarna-rupini).

She lives on great Kailasa (Mahakailasa-nilaya) and her arms are soft as lotus stems (Mrinala-mridu-dorlata). She is worthy of honour (Mahaniya), mercy in form (Dayamurti), and rules a great empire (Mahasamrajya-shalini).

She is knowledge of the Self (Atmavidya), the great knowledge (Mahavidya), Shri Vidya, and is served by Kama (Kamasevita). She is the sixteen-syllable mantra (Shrishodashakshari-vidya), has three parts (Trikuta), and dwells in Kamakoti (Kamakotika).

She is served by millions of Lakshmis who wait on her glance like servants (Kataksha-kinkari-bhuta-kamala-koti-sevita). She sits in the head, shining like the moon (Shirahsthita, Chandranibha), and in the forehead, glowing like a rainbow (Bhalastha, Indradhanuh-prabha).

She dwells in the heart, shining like the sun (Hridayastha, Raviprakhya), and is the lamp inside the triangle (Trikonantara-dipika). She is Dakshayani, kills demons (Daityahantri), and destroyed Daksha's sacrifice (Dakshayajna-vinashini).

Her long eyes move gently (Darandolita-dirghakshi) and her face glows with a soft smile (Darahasojjvala-mukhi). She is the guru in form (Gurumurti), a treasure of virtues (Gunanidhi), the mother of cows (Gomata), and the mother of Guha (Guhajanmabhuh).

She is the queen of the gods (Deveshi), upholds just rule (Dandanitistha), and is the small space within the heart (Daharakasha-rupini). She is worshipped on each lunar day, from the first to the full moon (Pratipan-mukhya-rakanta-tithi-mandala-pujita).

She is the arts in form (Kalatmika), the lord of the arts (Kalanatha), and enjoys poetry (Kavyalapa-vinodini). Lakshmi and Sarasvati attend her on the left and right, holding fans (Sachamara-rama-vani-savya-dakshina-sevita).

She is the first power (Adishakti), beyond measure (Ameya), the Self (Atma), supreme (Parama), and pure in form (Pavanakritih). She is the mother of countless millions of universes (Anekakoti-brahmanda-janani) and has a divine body (Divyavigraha).

She is the syllable Klim (Klimkari), the only one (Kevala), the secret one (Guhya), and gives final freedom (Kaivalya-pada-dayini). She is Tripura, worshipped in the three worlds (Trijagadvandya), the three gods in one (Trimurti), the queen of the gods (Tridasheshvari), the three-syllable mantra (Tryakshari), rich with divine fragrance (Divyagandhadhya), and marked with a vermilion dot (Sindura-tilakanchita). She is Uma, daughter of the king of mountains (Shailendratanaya), Gauri, and is served by the Gandharvas (Gandharva-sevita).

The universe lies in her womb (Vishvagarbha); she holds the golden womb (Svarnagarbha), she is Avarada, and she rules over speech (Vagadhishvari). She is reached by meditation (Dhyanagamya), has no limits (Aparichchhedya), gives knowledge (Jnanada), and is knowledge in form (Jnanavigraha).

She is known through all the Upanishads (Sarvavedanta-samvedya) and is truth and bliss (Satyananda-svarupini). She is worshipped by Lopamudra (Lopamudrarchita) and has made the universes as play (Lilaklripta-brahmanda-mandala).

She cannot be seen (Adrishya), there is nothing she needs to see (Drishyarahita), she knows all (Vijnatri), and nothing is left for her to know (Vedyavarjita). She is the yogini, gives yoga (Yogada), is reached by yoga (Yogya), is the joy of yoga (Yogananda), and upholds the ages (Yugandhara).

She is the power of will, the power of knowledge and the power of action (Ichchhashakti-jnanashakti-kriyashakti-svarupini). She is the support of all (Sarvadhara), firmly established (Supratishtha), and takes both real and unreal forms (Sadasadrupa-dharini).

She has eight forms (Ashtamurti), conquers ignorance (Ajajaitri), and directs the course of the world (Lokayatra-vidhayini). She is alone (Ekakini), the vast one (Bhumarupa), without a second (Nirdvaita), and beyond duality (Dvaitavarjita).

She gives food (Annada) and wealth (Vasuda), is ancient (Vriddha), and is the oneness of Brahman and the Self (Brahmatmaikya-svarupini). She is vast (Brihati), Brahmani, Brahmi, the bliss of Brahman (Brahmananda), and she loves offerings (Balipriya).

She is all languages (Bhasharupa), has a vast army (Brihatsena), and is beyond being and not-being (Bhavabhava-vivarjita). She is easy to worship (Sukharadhya), does good (Shubhakari), and is a lovely and easy path (Shobhana-sulabhagati).

She is the queen of the king of kings (Rajarajeshvari), gives kingdoms (Rajyadayini), and loves her kingdom (Rajyavallabha). Her mercy shines (Rajatkripa), and she seats on royal thrones those who rely on her (Rajapitha-niveshita-nijashrita).

She is the wealth of the kingdom (Rajyalakshmi), the lord of the treasury (Koshanatha), and commands the four-part army (Chaturanga-baleshvari). She gives empire (Samrajyadayini), keeps her word (Satyasandha), and wears the oceans as her girdle (Sagaramekhala).

She is consecrated (Dikshita), subdues demons (Daityashamani), and wins over all the worlds (Sarvaloka-vashankari). She gives every wish (Sarvarthadatri), is Savitri, and is being, consciousness and bliss (Sachchidananda-rupini).

She is not limited by place or time (Deshakala-parichchhinna), is everywhere (Sarvaga), and enchants all (Sarvamohini). She is Sarasvati, the scriptures in form (Shastramayi), the mother of Guha (Guhamba), and has a secret form (Guhyarupini).

She is free from every limit (Sarvopadhi-vinirmukta) and is the faithful wife of Sadashiva (Sadashiva-pativrata). She rules the line of tradition (Sampradayeshvari), is virtuous (Sadhvi), and is the circle of gurus in form (Gurumandala-rupini).

She is beyond the Kula (Kulottirna), worshipped in the Bhaga (Bhagaradhya), is Maya, sweet (Madhumati), and the earth (Mahi). She is the mother of the Ganas (Ganamba), worshipped by the Guhyakas (Guhyakaradhya), soft in body (Komalangi), and dear to the guru (Gurupriya).

She is free (Svatantra), rules all tantras (Sarvatantreshi), and has the form of Dakshinamurti. She is worshipped by Sanaka and the other sages (Sanakadi-samaradhya) and gives the knowledge of Shiva (Shivajnana-pradayini).

She is a spark of consciousness (Chitkala), a bud of bliss (Anandakalika), love itself (Premarupa), and does what is dear (Priyankari). She is pleased by recitation of her names (Namaparayana-prita), is Nandividya, and is the queen of the dancer Shiva (Nateshvari).

She is the base on which the unreal world rests (Mithyajagad-adhishthana), gives liberation (Muktida), and is liberation itself (Muktirupini). She loves graceful dance (Lasyapriya), dissolves all (Layakari), is modesty (Lajja), and is praised by Rambha and the other heavenly dancers (Rambhadi-vandita).

She is a rain of nectar on the forest fire of worldly life (Bhavadava-sudhavrishti) and a forest fire for the jungle of sins (Paparanya-davanala). She is a whirlwind for the cotton of bad luck (Daurbhagya-tulavatula) and sunlight for the darkness of old age (Jaradhvanta-raviprabha).

She is moonlight for the ocean of good fortune (Bhagyabdhi-chandrika) and a rain cloud for the peacocks that are her devotees' hearts (Bhaktachitta-keki-ghanaghana). She is a thunderbolt for the mountain of disease (Rogaparvata-dambholi) and an axe for the tree of death (Mrityudaru-kutharika).

She is the great ruler (Maheshvari), Mahakali, the great devourer (Mahagrasa) and the great eater (Mahashana). She is Aparna, Chandika, and the slayer of the demons Chanda and Munda (Chandamundasura-nishudini).

She is both the perishable and the imperishable (Ksharaksharatmika), the lord of all worlds (Sarvalokeshi), and holds up the universe (Vishvadharini). She gives the three goals of life (Trivargadatri), is fortunate (Subhaga), three-eyed (Tryambaka), and made of the three qualities (Trigunatmika).

She gives heaven and liberation (Svargapavargada), is pure (Shuddha), and her form is red like the hibiscus flower (Japapushpa-nibhakritih). She is full of vigour (Ojovati), holds light (Dyutidhara), is sacrifice in form (Yajnarupa), and loves sacred vows (Priyavrata).

She is hard to worship (Duraradhya), cannot be overcome (Duradharsha), and loves patali flowers (Patalikusuma-priya). She is great (Mahati), lives on Mount Meru (Merunilaya), and loves mandara flowers (Mandarakusuma-priya).

She is worshipped by heroes (Viraradhya), is the cosmic form (Viradrupa), is stainless (Viraja), and faces every way (Vishvatomukhi). She is the inner self (Pratyagrupa), the highest space (Parakasha), gives life (Pranada), and is life itself (Pranarupini).

She is worshipped by Martanda Bhairava (Martanda-bhairavaradhya) and has handed the burden of ruling to Mantrini (Mantrini-nyasta-rajyadhuh). She rules Tripura (Tripureshi), has a victorious army (Jayatsena), is beyond the three qualities (Nistraigunya), and is both the higher and the lower (Parapara).

She is truth, knowledge and bliss (Satyajnanananda-rupa) and is devoted to perfect oneness (Samarasya-parayana). She is the wife of Shiva of the matted hair (Kapardini), wears a garland of arts (Kalamala), grants every wish (Kamadhuk), and takes any form she wishes (Kamarupini).

She is a treasure of arts (Kalanidhi), the art of poetry (Kavyakala), knows every taste (Rasajna), and is a store of delight (Rasashevadhi). She is well nourished (Pushta), ancient (Puratana), worthy of worship (Pujya), the lotus (Pushkara), and lotus-eyed (Pushkarekshana).

She is the supreme light (Paramjyoti), the supreme home (Paramdhama), the finest atom (Paramanu), and higher than the highest (Paratpara). She holds the noose (Pashahasta), cuts all bonds (Pashahantri), and breaks the spells of enemies (Paramantra-vibhedini).

She has form and is also formless (Murta, Amurta), is ever content (Nityatripta), and is the swan in the minds of sages (Munimanasa-hamsika). She keeps her vows (Satyavrata), is truth itself (Satyarupa), the inner ruler of all (Sarvantaryamini), and is Sati.

She is Brahmani, the mother of Brahma (Brahmajanani), has many forms (Bahurupa), and is worshipped by the wise (Budharchita). She gives birth to all (Prasavitri), her command is fierce (Prachandajna), she is the foundation (Pratishtha), and her form is plain to see (Prakatakritih).

She is the lord of life (Praneshvari), gives life (Pranadatri), and is the fifty holy seats (Panchashatpitha-rupini). She is free of all chains (Vishrinkhala), lives in solitude (Viviktastha), is the mother of heroes (Viramata), and the source of space (Viyatprasuh).

She is Mukunda, the home of liberation (Muktinilaya), and the root form of all (Mulavigraha-rupini). She knows all feelings (Bhavajna), cures the disease of worldly life (Bhavarogaghni), and turns the wheel of births (Bhavachakra-pravartini).

She is the essence of the Vedas (Chhandahsara), of the scriptures (Shastrasara) and of the mantras (Mantrasara), and has a slender waist (Talodari). Her fame is noble (Udarakirti), her glory has no bounds (Uddamavaibhava), and her form is the letters (Varnarupini).

She gives rest to people worn out by birth, death and old age (Janmamrityu-jaratapta-jana-vishranti-dayini). All the Upanishads proclaim her (Sarvopanishad-udghushta), and she is the power that lies beyond peace (Shantyatita-kalatmika).

She is deep (Gambhira), lives within the sky (Gaganantastha), is proud (Garvita), and loves music (Ganalolupa). She is free of imagining (Kalpanarahita), the final limit (Kashtha), free of sin (Akanta), and half of her beloved's body (Kantardha-vigraha).

She is free of cause and effect (Karyakarana-nirmukta) and full of waves of love-play with Kameshvara (Kamakeli-tarangita). She wears shining gold earrings (Kanatkanaka-tatanka) and takes bodies in play (Lilavigraha-dharini).

She is unborn (Aja), free of decay (Kshayavinirmukta), innocent and charming (Mugdha), and quick to give grace (Kshipraprasadini). She is worshipped by those who turn inward (Antarmukha-samaradhya) and is very hard to reach for those who look outward (Bahirmukha-sudurlabha).

first: त्रयी त्रिवर्ग- निलया त्रिस्था त्रिपुर – मालिनी ।
en: She is the three Vedas (Trayi), the home of the three goals of life (Trivarganilaya), lives in the three worlds (Tristha), and wears the garland of Tripura (Tripuramalini). She is free of disease (Niramaya), needs no support (Niralamba), delights in her own Self (Svatmarama), and is a stream of nectar (Sudhasriti).

She is skilled at lifting out those sunk in the mud of worldly life (Samsarapanka-nirmagna-samuddharana-pandita). She loves sacrifice (Yajnapriya), performs it (Yajnakartri), and is the one who offers it (Yajamana-svarupini).

She is the support of dharma (Dharmadhara), the keeper of wealth (Dhanadhyaksha), and increases wealth and grain (Dhanadhanya-vivardhini). She loves the learned (Viprapriya), is the learned one (Viprarupa), and makes the universe turn (Vishvabhramana-karini).

She swallows the universe (Vishvagrasa), glows like coral (Vidrumabha), is Vaishnavi, and has Vishnu's form (Vishnurupini). She has no source (Ayoni), is the source of all (Yoninilaya), is unchanging (Kutastha), and is the Kula in form (Kularupini).

She loves the company of heroes (Viragoshthi-priya), is a heroine (Vira), is beyond action (Naishkarmya), and is sound in form (Nadarupini). She is the grasp of true knowledge (Vijnanakalana), able (Kalya), skilled (Vidagdha), and sits in the bindu (Baindavasana).

She is beyond the principles (Tattvadhika), made of them (Tattvamayi), and is the meaning of 'That' and 'you' (Tattvamartha-svarupini). She loves the chanting of the Sama Veda (Samagana-priya), is gentle (Saumya), and is the wife of Sadashiva (Sadashiva-kutumbini).

She stands on both the right and the left paths (Savyapasavya-margastha) and removes all dangers (Sarvapadvinivarini). She rests in herself (Svastha), is sweet by nature (Svabhavamadhura), wise and steady (Dhira), and worshipped by the wise (Dhirasamarchita).

She is worshipped with the offering of consciousness (Chaitanyarghya-samaradhya) and loves the flower of consciousness (Chaitanyakusuma-priya). She is always shining (Sadodita), always content (Sadatushta), and rosy like the young sun (Tarunaditya-patala).

She is worshipped on both the right and the left paths (Dakshinadakshinaradhya), and her lotus face smiles gently (Darasmera-mukhambuja). She is Kaulini, the only one (Kevala), and gives the priceless state of final freedom (Anarghya-kaivalya-pada-dayini).

She loves hymns (Stotrapriya), is worthy of praise (Stutimati), and her glory is praised by the Vedas (Shrutisamstuta-vaibhava). She is wise (Manasvini), dignified (Manavati), the great goddess (Maheshi), and auspicious in form (Mangalakritih).

She is the mother of the universe (Vishvamata), the upholder of the world (Jagaddhatri), wide-eyed (Vishalakshi), and free of passion (Viragini). She is bold (Pragalbha), most generous (Paramodara), full of supreme joy (Paramoda), and made of mind (Manomayi).

The sky is her hair (Vyomakeshi); she rides a heavenly chariot (Vimanastha), holds the thunderbolt (Vajrini), and is Vamakeshvari. She loves the five sacrifices (Panchayajna-priya) and rests on a couch made of five lifeless forms (Panchapreta-manchadhishayini).

She is Panchami, the ruler of the five elements (Panchabhuteshi), and is worshipped with five offerings (Panchasankhyopacharini). She is eternal (Shashvati), her lordship is eternal (Shashvataishvarya), she gives happiness (Sharmada), and she charms Shambhu (Shambhumohini).

She is the earth (Dhara), the daughter of the mountain (Dharasuta), blessed (Dhanya), righteous (Dharmini), and increases dharma (Dharmavardhini). She is beyond the worlds (Lokatita), beyond qualities (Gunatita), beyond all (Sarvatita), and peace itself (Shamatmika).

She glows like the red bandhuka flower (Bandhuka-kusuma-prakhya), is the young girl Bala, and delights in play (Lilavinodini). She is fully auspicious (Sumangali), gives joy (Sukhakari), is finely dressed (Suveshadhya), and is a happily married woman (Suvasini).
She is pleased by the worship of married women (Suvasinyarchana-prita), is radiant (Ashobhana), and has a pure mind (Shuddhamanasa).
She is pleased by offerings to the bindu (Bindu-tarpana-santushta), is the first-born (Purvaja), and is Tripurambika, the mother of Tripura.

She is worshipped with the ten mudras (Dashamudra-samaradhya) and holds Tripurashri in her power (Tripurashri-vashankari). She is the mudra of knowledge (Jnanamudra), reached by knowledge (Jnanagamya), and is both knowledge and what is known (Jnanajneya-svarupini).

She is the yoni mudra (Yonimudra), the ruler of the three parts (Trikhandeshi), the mother of the three qualities (Trigunamba), and dwells in the triangle (Trikonaga). She is sinless (Anagha), her deeds are wonderful (Adbhutacharitra), and she grants what one wishes for (Vanchhitartha-pradayini).

She is known through long and steady practice (Abhyasatishaya-jnata) and is beyond the six paths (Shadadhvatita-rupini). She is mercy that needs no reason (Avyajakaruna-murti) and a lamp in the darkness of ignorance (Ajnanadhvanta-dipika).

She is known to all, even children and cowherds (Abalagopa-vidita), and no one can disobey her command (Sarvanullanghya-shasana). She lives in the Shri Chakra (Shrichakraraja-nilaya) and is the holy Tripurasundari (Shrimat-tripurasundari).

She is the holy auspicious one (Shrishiva), the oneness of Shiva and Shakti (Shivashaktyaikya-rupini), and Lalitambika. In this way the goddesses of speech sang the thousand names of the goddess Shri Lalita.
Here ends the hymn of the thousand names of Shri Lalita, from the dialogue of Shri Hayagriva and Agastya in the last part of the Brahmanda Purana.
